message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to finish a round and by collecting the cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”, two “Draw Two”) + 4 “Wild” + 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two cards and loses a turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players sit in a circle. The first player is the one to the left of the dealer. Turn order moves clockwise unless a “Reverse” card is played, which flips the direction. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top card on the discard pile. If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | 1. **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
2. **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
3. **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
4. **Wild** – You choose the new color.
5. **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card (i.e., you have one card left), you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by the other players: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points each, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points each. | | **Winning the Game** | The first player to reach the target score (commonly 500) wins. If you’re playing a shorter game, you can set a lower target or play a single round. | | **House Variations** | • **Draw‑Four Challenge** – If you suspect a player illegally played a Wild Draw Four, they can challenge. If the challenger is right, the player who played the card draws 4 cards; if wrong, the challenger draws 6 cards.
• **Stacking** – Some groups allow “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” to be stacked: a player can play another of the same type to pass the penalty onto the next player.
• **No “Draw Four” on the first turn** – Some rules forbid playing a Wild Draw Four as the first card of a round. | --- ### Quick Play‑through Example 1. **Deal**: Each player gets 7 cards. 2. **Start**: Flip top card – say it’s a Red 5. 3. **Player A** (first to play) has a Red 9 → plays it. 4. **Player B** has a Yellow 9 → plays it. 5. **Player C** has a “Skip” → plays it; Player D loses a turn. 6. **Player E** has a “Wild” → plays it, chooses Green. 7. **Player F** has no green or wild → draws a card. If it’s playable, they play it; otherwise, turn ends. 8. Continue until someone discards their last card. --- ### Tips for New Players - **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on a particular color, try to play a Wild to change the color to something you have more of. - **Watch the discard pile** – Knowing what cards have been played helps you anticipate what your opponents might hold. - **Use “Draw Two” and “Wild Draw Four” strategically** – Save them for when you’re about to win or when you need to block an opponent. - **Remember “UNO”** – It’s a simple rule but can cost you two cards if you forget! Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
